project.name: Blinky
project.tagline: Your key blinks. Blinky is why.

status.summary: Phase 2, the gate is met. On 2026-08-24, jnowak@blinky.lab logged in to BY-WIN-CLIENT01 with a YubiKey carrying a certificate this system issued - own two-tier CA, own directory lookup for the UPN and objectSid, own agent, Samba4 KDC over PKINIT, and no ADCS anywhere. The card was fully personalised first: management key derived per token and stored nowhere, PIN chosen by the holder, PUK replaced and escrowed. Both unblock paths were exercised, online and offline. Two findings worth carrying. Windows' inbox PIV minidriver would not produce a key container for a card meeting every requirement in SP 800-73 that could be checked; Yubico's minidriver did, and is a prerequisite for the workstation - but it takes ownership of any card whose management key it does not recognise, which is why 0025 writes the key behind the PIN and sets the flag Yubico's tools read. And a certificate chain trusted for TLS is not thereby trusted for logon: the issuing CA must be in the workstation's NTAuth store, and Windows reports its absence as CERT_E_UNTRUSTEDCA, which reads exactly like a broken chain. Fourteen defects surfaced over the day, most of them this project's own. Three are worth naming: the installer protected every CA private key with the literal password "blinky" while .env recorded a strong one that opened nothing; 7F49 was parsed as a tag plus a length rather than the two-byte tag it is, which broke every RSA issuance and was hidden by a hard-coded ECC algorithm; and the issuing CA never received a CRL distribution point at all, because the script that adds one refused to run and the installer swallowed the refusal through a grep and a || true. Still open: an orphaned Issued credential from an earlier attempt, the API gaps in doc 11 that block enrolment from the console, reconciliation (0029), and a card cannot be personalised without also being issued to.

phases.title: Design
phases.done: Solution builds, schema script creates the PostgreSQL schema, SchemaValidator reports clean at service start.

phases.title: See the token
phases.done: Three different YubiKeys - factory, ykman-provisioned, blocked PIN - each report correct state in the database, with no write to any card.

phases.title: Issue something
phases.done: docker compose up, enrol a factory YubiKey from the console, and log into a Samba4 domain with it. No ADCS involved.

phases.title: ADCS
phases.done: The same workflow, console and audit trail against Windows AD plus ADCS, differing only in the profile's CA instance.

phases.title: The boring lifecycle
phases.done: Expiry produces exactly one renewal job; revocation regenerates and publishes the CRL; a blocked PIN is unblocked from an escrowed PUK with an audited disclosure.

phases.title: Console
phases.done: Every token and credential state is visible and explained; a credential's whole life is reconstructable from the audit view alone.

phases.title: Ship it
phases.done: A stranger can go from clone to smart-card logon using only the repository.

phases.title: The workstation app, and signing in
phases.done: A user on a domain workstation and a user on a machine with no domain each open the app, sign in their own way, and enrol a card they asked for; an operator enrols on behalf of a third person through the same ceremony; and an administrator signs into the panel with a password and a TOTP code, having been forced to set the second factor before anything else. Numbered after phase 7 and not thereby scheduled after it.

phases.title: FIDO2 on the same key
phases.done: An operator provisions a fresh YubiKey from the console for an Entra lab-tenant user and for an Okta lab-org user; each signs in at their own provider with that key; the provisional PIN must be changed on first use; revoking from the console removes the method at the provider; every step is in the audit trail; unit and contract tests green with no hardware, no tenant and no org.

phases.title: S/MIME on the card and on the phone
phases.done: One person, one mailbox. Outlook on Windows signs and decrypts with the card; Boxer on a UEM-managed phone reads a message encrypted to that card before the phone existed and signs a reply the desktop accepts; a lost card is replaced from escrow and the old mail still opens on both; terminating the person revokes the card's certificates and the phone's together. Design in docs/16.

decisions.choice: Angular in a Tauri v2 shell, replacing the WPF tray; one UI technology for the whole product, and the same components as the console
A loopback HTTPS API on the agent, not the named pipe - chosen for shape, at the cost of an ACL the operating system was enforcing, with four checks in 0080 to rebuild it
Full CRUD for anything describing configuration or people; create-and-transition for anything recording an event
.NET 10
PC/SC with raw PIV APDUs; no PKCS#11 module, no CLI wrapper
YubiKey 5 PIV only in v1
Built-in CA and ADCS behind one interface, both from the start
.NET for signing, BouncyCastle only for CMC and PKCS#7
PKCS#11 abstraction with file, SoftHSM2 and HSM tiers
Per-token HKDF derivation from an HSM-held master; no key material in the database
PINs are never stored in any form
Random per token, AES-256-GCM under an HSM KEK, disclosure audited
HTTPS REST plus a stateless SignalR doorbell; no broker
LocalSystem service plus per-session UI process
Agent proves the machine with mTLS; the user proves themselves with Kerberos from their own session
PostgreSQL with NHibernate, SQL schema script, SchemaValidator at startup
Angular 22 behind nginx with /api proxied
Apache-2.0
Built-in CA as a library inside api and worker, or its own service
Whether desk-side PIN unblock works without the backend
YubiKey Bio Multi-protocol is a first-class target; biometrics detected by asking slot 96, never inferred from the model
Bio tokens accepted with puk_state=NotApplicable; non-Bio tokens with a deleted PUK refused unless AllowUnrecoverableTokens
nginx + ModSecurity 3 + CRS v4 in the frontend container; console listener blocking, agent listener DetectionOnly with mTLS
Built-in CA runs as single or two-tier, chosen per CA instance, default two-tier; topology is immutable once set
Own LibraryImport into winscard.dll rather than a NuGet wrapper; Windows-only until pcsc-lite marshalling can be tested (patch 0017)
Pin only the Yubico root, embedded with its SHA-256 checked at load; the per-device intermediate is read from the card and verified
The schema is generated from the mappings by tools/SchemaTool; a CI test fails when the committed file stops matching
The edge asks for a client certificate (optional) and the API requires one on every path except enrolment
A separate CA issues agent client certificates; short-lived and rotated
Agents report what the card said; the server decides what it means
Detected by asking the card for a serial, never by reader name; reported as unsupported with a reason rather than skipped
The WebAuthn ceremony runs in the agent over CTAP2, never in the browser
rpId and origin are per-provider, per-tenant data carried in the job payload, never constants in code
Generated on the workstation, shown to the operator once, stored nowhere; delivered by the provider instead where the provider can
Entra ID and Okta behind one interface; Google Workspace analysed and not built, because no API accepts an attestation on behalf of a user

openQuestions.question: What exact CES authentication and delegation configuration is required for RA-signed enrol-on-behalf-of?
Does operator authentication by certificate stay the target, with password and TOTP as the way in - or does it become optional?
openQuestions.needs: a decision. It settles whether 0023a's enrolment-agent signature names a person or a service, which is the difference between cryptographic evidence and an audit line. On the table: superadmin keeps password and TOTP forever because it is the way back in when nothing else works, and operator moves to a certificate once operators have cards

openQuestions.question: Do non-Yubico PIV tokens get a capability model - attestation yes/no, management key yes/no - and may a profile issue onto a token that cannot attest?
openQuestions.needs: measurement with InsProbe, then a decision. Today the answer is 'recognised and refused', which is correct and is not a plan

openQuestions.question: Should the built-in CA run as its own process so the key material sits behind a process boundary?
Should desk-side PIN unblock work offline with a pre-fetched, time-boxed PUK?
Ship a CLI-first v1 and defer the Angular console?
Which HSM in production, and does it need to hold the master key and the CA key in the same partition?
Does the lab get an Entra tenant and an Okta org, or does Phase 7 stop at contract tests against recorded fixtures?
Is Google Workspace worth a prepare-only mode - PIN preset, hand-off sheet, read-only compliance loop - or is federating Google behind Entra or Okta the whole answer?

risks.handling: Validated 2026-08-19 on firmware 5.4.3 next to HID ActivClient: shared connection plus transaction, no contention. Hardware suite from patch 0011 keeps it honest
Read GET METADATA, fall back once, record Unknown rather than guessing
Backend registration refuses the combination up front
Verified as part of the phase 2 gate
Guard inside the agent step, not only in the server retry policy
Shared PC/SC connections inside transactions, never exclusive
AwaitingUser is a distinct state with its own longer deadline
Patch 0016 reads it, 0027 uses it; the temporary-PIN encoding is marked unverified in doc 03
PcscContext.IsSupported plus an explicit PlatformNotSupportedException; patch 0017
6Cxx needs a T=0 reader and outbound chaining needs a write; hand-built cases cover both until patch 0024
Microsoft Graph's fido2Methods endpoints are beta. Isolated behind IPasskeyDirectory, with recorded fixtures so a contract change surfaces as a failing test rather than as a broken deployment
A FIDO reset destroys every discoverable credential and there is no PUK equivalent. 0070 makes them visible before 0072 can destroy them, and the reset needs a confirmation naming the count
Options are fetched only after the key has answered; expiry is a retryable code with a fresh challenge, and for Okta the pending factor is deleted before the retry
Deliberate, and the reason Okta's ProviderDelivers mode is worth having: the PIN is emailed to the holder and passes through no operator and no database

Phase 7 is the first thing here that needs the internet. Only the api container reaches graph.microsoft.com, login.microsoftonline.com or the Okta org URL; the rest of the stack stays on-premises, and 0079 documents it

patches.title: Enrol on behalf of, for the built-in CA
patches.proof: Essential. An operator asking for a certificate in somebody else's name is the normal case, and today the only thing between that request and a certificate asserting a stranger's identity is a shared token in a header - with a record of who asked that the same token could have written. ADCS answers this with an enrolment agent's signature on the request, which 0030 uses; the built-in CA has no equivalent. Buildable before 0053a and worth less until it lands: the format, the signature check and the EKU rule can exist now, but naming which operator asked waits for operators to hold certificates.

patches.title: Personalisation: management key, PUK escrow, PIN policy
patches.proof: On 2026-08-24, token 29051525 (firmware 5.7.1) went from factory to fully personalised and was used to log in to Windows for half an hour. ykman piv info reports no default management key and no default PIN, and prints 'Management key is stored on the YubiKey, protected by PIN'. The management key is derived per token from a master and written nowhere; the PIN was chosen by the holder under protest of the enrolment, which refuses a card still on the factory value; the PUK was replaced and escrowed. Both unblock paths were exercised on that card - online through the agent, and offline by reading a challenge to an operator and typing the answer back - and the audit distinguishes them by actor and reason.
patches.gap: The master can now live in a token rather than in .env - see 0025a - but the default is still .env, so a deployment that has not provisioned one reports productionReady false. A card is personalised only at its first enrolment, so every card issued before this keeps its factory management key and PUK and cannot be brought in without wiping it. There is no way to personalise a card without also issuing to it, which means a card already carrying a working credential cannot have its PIN or PUK replaced.

patches.title: The master secrets behind PKCS#11, with SoftHSM2 as the reference module
patches.proof: src/Blinky.Secrets holds one interface with one operation - a keyed MAC computed where the key lives - and no way to ask for a key. Two providers behind it: Configuration, which is the arrangement that existed before and is still the default, and Pkcs11, which is a module path and a token label. Keys are separated by purpose and by generation with derived labels, the provider discovers every generation up to the configured one so a rotation can overlap, and it reads CKA_SENSITIVE and CKA_EXTRACTABLE back from the token and refuses a key the device would hand out. Use is counted and logged with neither input nor output, and reported per key on /api/system/status alongside which provider answered. The HKDF extract half moved out of the process because a token holding the master as a key cannot perform it; the token holds the extract instead, which for a 32-byte output makes the derivation bit-for-bit what it was, so an existing deployment imports the extract of its current master and every card keeps the key it holds. That equality is pinned by a test. Token.ManagementKeyVersion is written for the first time, which also fixes diversified cards reading back as Lost. Run for the first time against a real module on 2026-09-12, in a container on BY-CACMS: eleven PKCS#11 tests pass and none skips, including the refusal of an extractable key and the equality between an imported master and the configured one. 423 unit tests pass on Windows.
patches.gap: Two things stay unproved and neither is the token path. The compose wiring and the Dockerfile change were exercised by hand on BY-CACMS - the tool provisioned a token in the api image and the API started against the configuration provider - but no automated check covers them. And the PUK escrow needed a real transition rather than a compatible one, because the KEK was used directly as a cipher key: generation two derives a key per envelope, generation one stays readable through the configured KEK, and Blinky:Puk:Kek has to stay set for as long as any generation-one envelope exists. Nothing re-wraps them. The CA issuing key is not part of this - it is still the file tier, and 0021 owns it. Running the whole suite on Linux also fails UserPromptTests twice, which is the agent named-pipe pair and fails identically on b9b2285.

patches.title: Master secrets status in the system console
patches.proof: The /system console renders secrets separately from CA key custody: provider and reported readiness, configured write generations checked against all reported keys, extractability, per-process usage, factory management-key mode and legacy PUK readability. Labels are available in Polish and English, with light and dark theme styles. Production Angular build passes; all 19 frontend tests pass, including five rendered-panel scenarios for old APIs, missing generations, unsafe exportability, readiness, factory keys and translations.
patches.gap: Not yet verified after signing in to /system on BY-CACMS against the deployed API; light and dark layouts still require visual verification. No API or hardware changes.

patches.title: AdcsCertificateAuthority and CMC with an EA signature
patches.proof: Blinky.Pki/Adcs exists: IAdcsTransport with the connector's wire contract as its vocabulary rather than a translated one, AdcsCertificateAuthority written once for both transports, CmcRequest, and IEnrolmentAgentKeyStore. Capabilities are not hopeful - PublishesCrl false because ADCS keeps its own list, SupportsSuppliedSubject false because a template that takes the subject from the request emits no SID extension, SupportsRevocation taken from what the CA said about Issue and Manage Certificates. UnderSubmission raises its own IssuancePendingException carrying the request id, because a request waiting for a certificate manager is neither a success nor a refusal and folding it into either loses a certificate. The CMC is hand-encoded against RFC 5272 - .NET has no CMC type and certenroll is COM - and the tests assert the four sequences, the [0] implicit tag and the cardholder's PKCS#10 byte for byte inside the agent's signature. The template is not in the CMC: it travels in the attribute string both ICertRequest3 and CES already accept. Twenty-seven tests, no CA needed. The enrolment agent key question is settled and written down: a sibling of ICaKeyStore rather than a third KeyPurpose, because IKeyProvider computes an HMAC and a CMS SignerInfo is not one; FileEnrolmentAgentKeyStore refuses to load without Blinky:Adcs:AllowFileKeys and refuses a certificate ADCS would refuse - no private key, out of date, or no Certificate Request Agent EKU, absent EKU extension included. docs/06-security.md now ranks this key second in the custody list. The EOBO shape from MS-WCCE is written. CmcRequest puts a RegInfo control (body part 2, requestername=DOMAIN\user, nothing else) before the PKCS#10. The connector and the file store both add a no-signature SignerInfo beside the agent's, and a test holds the two shapes equal. PkiDataInspection accepts exactly one RegInfo with a well-formed requester name and refuses any other control. AdcsCertificateAuthority refuses to issue without CardholderIdentity.LogonName, before the agent is opened. On HZCS01 the connector ran as the service BlinkyAdcsConnector (LocalSystem) against SUBCA\DigitalWorkspace Issuing CA - homelab, which showed that Connector:CaConfig was documented and never read; fixed. Definition of done met on 2026-09-13: with the connector service running as AD\svc_blinky, tools/AdcsProbe --submit BlinkySmartCardLogon --remote-agent --requester AD\BlinkyUser sent a CMC built by CmcRequest and signed by the connector, and SUBCA\DigitalWorkspace Issuing CA - homelab issued serial 47000000097012D4FEBA5C0A0E000000000009. The CA ignored the requested CN=BlinkyUser and built the subject (CN=BlinkyUser, OU=Users, OU=DIGITALWORKSPACE, DC=ad, DC=digitalworkspace, DC=pl), the UPN BlinkyUser@ad.digitalworkspace.pl and the SID extension from the directory object requestername named, so the RegInfo control and the SignerInfo order as DER encodes it are both accepted. The first attempt, with a P-256 key, was denied with CERTSRV_E_KEY_LENGTH because the template is on the default cryptography settings; RSA 2048 issued.
patches.gap: Outside this definition of done and recorded so it is not lost: the API fills CardholderIdentity.LogonName at issuance through ADCS (LogonNames: sAMAccountName for the enrolment's UPN, checked against its SID, and the NetBIOS name from the domain's crossRef or Blinky:Directory:NetBiosDomain), unit-tested and not yet run against a directory, and no card has been enrolled through ADCS from the console. The lab template refuses ECC P-256 card keys as too short. A PKCS#11 enrolment agent key store for CES does not exist.

patches.title: CES/CEP transport
Blinky.AdcsConnector over DCOM
patches.proof: Both ends of the wire exist and talk to each other, and the enrolment agent's key lives on the Windows side. The connector is a Windows service listening over mutual TLS, authorising callers by SHA-256 fingerprint and refusing to start with an empty allowlist, calling ICertRequest3 and ICertAdmin2 by late binding; COM calls are serialised and a timed-out call keeps the lock. It holds the enrolment agent in the integration account's store and signs a PKIData the container built, after refusing anything that is not exactly one PKCS#10 enrolment - no controls, since a control can be a signed revocation; no nested content; no second request; no request whose own signature fails - and logs subject, key hash and calling client certificate for every signature. The key moved there from the container on purpose: in a Windows store it can be non-exportable or in a TPM, the CA server is already the most trusted machine, and the only container tier was an exported PKCS#12. Custody is read off the key: the same PKCS#12 imported twice gave one exportable key and one not, depending only on the import flag, so the connector reports the key's own export policy. ConnectorAdcsTransport has no accept-anything option and refuses a SHA-1 thumbprint where a SHA-256 fingerprint belongs. The certificate rules are duplicated in the connector and the container, and a test runs the same certificates through both. Checkable by somebody who did not write it: with the connector holding the agent on a machine with no CA, tools/AdcsProbe --remote-agent has the connector sign a PKIData built in the container and carries the CMC into ICertRequest3::Submit, which answers RPC_S_SERVER_UNAVAILABLE; the connector's log records the signature with the key hash and the caller. The API can be pointed at it: Blinky:Ca:Backend=Adcs builds AdcsCertificateAuthority from AdcsInstanceOptions, which is the shape CaInstance.Configuration is meant to take and holds no key material. Local mistakes stop the process at start with a sentence - verified by starting the API and the worker with an unknown backend and with Transport=Ces - and the enrolment agent is opened at the first enrolment, so the API starts while the CA server reboots. /api/system/status reports an unreachable CA instead of returning 500. The worker does nothing for an ADCS CA, because MaintenanceRunner would re-revoke every revoked certificate at the CA every cycle. On HZCS01, a Windows Server 2022 domain member with no CA role and no .NET, a self-contained build reached through an SSH tunnel loaded the lab's real computer-bound enrolment agent from LocalMachine\My by fingerprint, reported it non-exportable in agreement with certutil, and signed a CMC with it. Three defects found there and fixed: a PKCS#12 could not be imported into the user key set in a key-authenticated session, because DPAPI had no credential; the revocation-permission probe read an RPC failure against a missing CA as revocation available, because certadm.dll ships with Windows Server; and a local account's failure to read the directory said only that the domain does not exist.
patches.gap: The choice is configuration and not yet the database: CA instances and profiles are not read from it, so a deployment has one CA and templates are mapped per profile in Blinky:Adcs:Templates - 0022's open half - and CaInstance.Configuration is still "{}" with no CRUD. The compose and .env keys exist and the compose file was edited without Docker to parse it. No installer, and no client certificate for the API - which is now the most sensitive file in the container, since it buys the agent's signature. The integration account is not designed yet and has to be: Enroll on the agent and card templates, the agent certificate generated in its own store, and Issue and Manage Certificates confined by certificate manager restrictions rather than granted CA-wide - docs/15 section 7. On HZCS01 the connector runs as the service BlinkyAdcsConnector, now as AD\svc_blinky, reaches the lab CA and the forest, and got a certificate issued (0030). The account is the lab's hybrid of the two designed arrangements: a domain account with a password, using the computer-bound agent key.

patches.title: The connector dials the API
patches.proof: Decided 2026-09-13 at the lab owner's request: an inbound rule into the CA's network is the one a tiered estate refuses. ConnectorQueue in Blinky.Pki holds calls for a connector to collect, with a 20-second pickup deadline that names when a connector last polled and a 90-second answer deadline; a call abandoned before collection is never handed out, and a late answer is refused with 410. ConnectorAdcsTransport is unchanged but for a handler that queues the request instead of sending it, so the contract checks and error sentences are shared with the direct transport. Blinky:Adcs:Transport=ConnectorPolls selects it, and it refuses to build without Blinky:Adcs:Connector:ClientFingerprints. The API serves GET /api/adcs/connector/next (long poll, 25 s) and POST /api/adcs/connector/result; AgentAuthenticationMiddleware accepts only the listed fingerprints there, before and instead of the agent lookup. The connector, given Connector:Api:Url, opens no listener, and runs each collected call through its own /connector/* endpoints in memory through TestServer, refusing any other path or method. scripts/new-connector-request.ps1 and scripts/sign-connector-cert.sh give it a non-exportable key and a certificate from the agent CA; the signing script was run against a throwaway CA with a CRLF request. Against the lab CA, with AdcsProbe --queue playing the API through ssh -R: describe, the registration check, a P-256 issuance for AD\BlinkyUser and its revocation all went through the queue, logged by the connector as asked by the API. The first run found every POST refused with an empty 400, because TestServer decides whether a request may have a body before the body is set; fixed and tested. Twenty new tests. Then through the real edge and API on BY-CACMS: the connector's certificate from the agent CA, accepted on HZCS01 without trusting that CA, reached by name over TLS; before the fingerprint was configured the API refused it as not a connector's, after it the long poll answered 204 at 25 seconds through nginx, and the console's status page answered in about 40 ms through the connector. The scripts were fixed on the way: the signing script now shows openssl's error and checks the key is readable, and the request script falls back to certutil -addstore and -repairstore on CERT_E_CHAINING. On 2026-09-14 a card was enrolled through it end to end: tools/lab-enrol.ps1 against the API on BY-CACMS created the cardholder s.frankiewicz from ad.digitalworkspace.pl and asked the agent on VDF001 to enrol YubiKey 5.8.0 serial 39218739; the agent generated and attested the key, the API resolved AD\s.frankiewicz, the connector on HZCS01 collected the sign and submit calls over 9443, SUBCA issued serial 470000000E66720890519367F500000000000E with the subject taken from the directory, the agent wrote it to slot 9A, and smart-card logon to VDF001 over RDP succeeded. Defects found and fixed on the way: /pki/root.crt answered 404 under ADCS so a workstation could not trust the edge; the console's status polling queued describes behind each other past four seconds, now cached for 30 seconds; the compose entrypoint's shell dropped the hyphenated template variable.
patches.gap: Suspending the credential from the console and seeing the CA list it as held (step 9 of the plan in docs/09) has not been run. The console has no enrolment page, so the card was enrolled through the API with a lab script. The revocation-permission probe still calls the CA on every describe, every 30 seconds with the cache - issue #3. The queue is in memory, so an API restart loses calls in flight, including a submission the CA may already have issued. One API replica only. The unit tests for the last changes (attestation root, PIN re-verification, describe cache) could not run on the development machine, whose Smart App Control refuses the locally built Blinky.Secrets.dll.

patches.title: Backend registration checks
patches.proof: AdcsRegistration returns named findings with stable codes, reachable as GET /api/system/ca/checks and tools/AdcsProbe --check. The three refusals the definition of done names each have a test: a template whose msPKI-Certificate-Name-Flag supplies the subject, an enrolment agent that is missing or expired, and an account the template's security descriptor does not grant Enroll - evaluated against the account's token groups, with Full Control and all-extended-rights counted as grants and a matching deny winning. Also refused: no authorized signature, a signature under the wrong application policy, a template not published on the CA or not in the forest. The connector reads the template object as the integration account through GET /connector/templates/{name}. Three outcomes rather than a bool: the first version counted refusals only and, run against a connector with no CA and no domain behind it, reported the registration accepted with nothing verified; Unknown is its own severity now and the same run reports Unverified with the CA's missing certificate and the unreadable template named. Against the lab forest, through the connector running as AD\Administrator on HZCS01: the template BlinkyEnrollmentAgent(Computer) was found and every attribute read, including through a name with parentheses, and refused for requiring no authorised signature - correct for an agent template, which was read because the smart-card template's name was not yet known. Through the service as LocalSystem on HZCS01, against the real smart-card template BlinkySmartCardLogon: schema 4, name flags 0x82000000, one authorised signature under the Certificate Request Agent policy in the version 4 encoding MS-CRTD describes, and every attribute check passed. The first run refused account-cannot-enroll for NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM, because the Enroll check evaluated the local S-1-5-18 token. LocalSystem and NetworkService are now judged as the computer object - its objectSid, its tokenGroups and the well-known logon groups - and the same check finds Enroll for AD\HZCS01$ and ends Unverified with revocation-unavailable and template-publication-unknown. The revocation probe discriminates: 0x80070057 as AD\Administrator, 0x80070005 as HZCS01$. The template's minimum key size is now read (msPKI-Minimal-Key-Size, additive on AdcsTemplateInfo) and set against the key algorithms the deployment enrols with, Blinky:Adcs:KeyAlgorithms or all five: template-key-too-short is a refusal when nothing gets through and a warning when some do, and template-key-algorithm warns when a version 4 template names another algorithm. Against BlinkySmartCardLogon through the redeployed connector it warns that ECCP256 and ECCP384 will be denied with CERTSRV_E_KEY_LENGTH, which is what the CA did to a P-256 key the day before. With the template then moved to a Key Storage Provider, ECDH_P256 and a 256-bit minimum, a P-256 key and an RSA 2048 key were both issued for AD\BlinkyUser and both revoked through the connector: the CA enforces the minimum size and not the named algorithm, so template-key-algorithm stays a warning and now says so from observation. Read back afterwards with AdcsProbe --retrieve: the P-256 certificate from the ECDH_P256 template carries digital signature and key agreement, so it may sign a PKINIT request; the RSA one from the same template carries digital signature only, and the first, from the legacy template, digital signature and key encipherment.
patches.gap: No registration flow exists to refuse anything: CA instances are not database rows until 0022's open half, so the check runs on request against the one CA configuration names. Template publication stays unknown when the connector is not on the CA, because the list is in the CA's registry. The revocation probe has been read against one CA version with two identities. Restricted Enrollment Agents and certificate manager restrictions are not detected, so they cannot yet be recommended with evidence.

patches.title: Revocation through ADCS
patches.gap: Nothing has been revoked from the console, and the CA's CDP is not surfaced. The CA records every revocation as made by AD\svc_blinky, so who asked exists only in Blinky's audit event, and that event has only been built and compiled - no API with a database has written one yet. The lab grant is CA-wide with no certificate manager restrictions, and the design in docs/15 section 7 still says to confine it before production. SupportsRevocation follows describe's AdminAvailable, which cannot tell an account without the grant from a machine without ICertAdmin2.
patches.proof: Revocation at a real CA through the path the API uses: AdcsProbe --revoke called AdcsCertificateAuthority.RevokeAsync, the connector ran ICertAdmin2::RevokeCertificate as AD\svc_blinky against SUBCA\DigitalWorkspace Issuing CA - homelab, and the CA accepted the revocation of the test certificate 47000000097012D4FEBA5C0A0E000000000009 with reason cessation of operation. The connector logs every revocation with the serial, the reason and the fingerprint of the calling client certificate, because an account holding Issue and Manage Certificates CA-wide can revoke anything the CA holds. Two more test certificates, one P-256 and one RSA 2048, were revoked the same way minutes after issuance. Read back through the connector, which now returns the certificate of a revoked request too: all three requests answer Revoked by AD\svc_blinky. Blinky's own record of who revoked did not exist: CredentialIssuanceService.RevokeAsync wrote no audit event for a revocation, a suspension or a token blocked as lost. It now writes credential.revoked with the actor, serial, reason, comment and CA in the same transaction, exempt from retention, and lifting a suspension writes token.unblocked.

patches.title: Writing to the directory: userCertificate and altSecurityIdentities
patches.proof: Someday, and off by default. Writing needs a second credential with write access to user objects; the read path stays on the account that has none, which is the whole value of the read design - a read-only account is easy to ask for and easy to audit. Only strong mappings: X509IssuerSerialNumber, X509SKI, X509SHA1PublicKey. The weak forms are what KB5014754 disabled and writing one would be this product undoing the protection it exists to enforce. Not the route to a second identity on one card: the smartcard-logon profile embeds the holder's SID, which is the extension that stops A's certificate logging on as B, so a mapping on an administrative account collides with it rather than sidestepping it. Two certificates in two slots need no mapping and no delegation. This is for the certificate that cannot carry the right identity - an external CA, a forest boundary, a migration.

patches.title: Expiry scanner and scheduled renewal
Revocation, CRL regeneration and publication
An OCSP responder, and the address that is already in the certificates
patches.proof: Half of it is done and is the half that cannot wait: CaPublication carries OcspUrls, BuiltInCertificateAuthority emits authority information access when either list is non-empty, and Blinky:Ca:OcspUrl configures it. Unset in every deployment, because nothing answers OCSP yet and a certificate advertising a responder that does not exist is worse than one advertising none.
patches.gap: No responder. The address exists early because authority information access is fixed at issuance and cannot be added to a card afterwards - deciding it later means re-issuing to everyone holding one.

patches.title: PIN unblock via escrowed PUK, with audit
Lost, stolen, terminate, retire
Stale-slot detection and reconciliation
Retired-slot rotation for 9D
Escrow for the 9D key
patches.proof: The encryption key is generated centrally, escrowed and imported onto the card - the opposite of 9A and 9C and correct for the opposite reason. A key that only ever existed on a card makes every message encrypted to it unreadable the moment the card is lost, and rotation does not bring it back. Needs a key import path in Blinky.Piv, which does not exist at all today.

patches.title: Tray-resident agent UI and the certificate list
patches.proof: The tray lists what is on the token beside what the backend holds, in Polish and English, light and dark. It holds no PC/SC handle and caches no card state between openings. Two defects found by running it that no test caught: a refresh dropped while another was in flight, and a window closed rather than hidden, which WPF will not show again.

patches.title: PIN set and change from the workstation, with a complexity policy
patches.proof: The policy travels from the backend and is enforced in the service, never only in the window. A refusal for being too simple consumes no card attempt and is worded differently from a mismatch and from 63CN.

patches.title: Unblock from the workstation: just-in-time PUK, used once, rotated after
patches.proof: The PUK reaches the service and never the UI or the disk; the disclosure is audited and the PUK rotated immediately after use.

patches.title: Unblock over a telephone, for a workstation with no network
patches.proof: Verified on hardware over two cycles: the agent shows a challenge, an operator answers it, and both sides derive the replacement PUK without exchanging it. A mistyped code is refused before it reaches the card, with the attempt counter untouched. Unreachable from the logon screen, which is what 0049a is for.

patches.title: Renewal requested by the user
patches.proof: The new certificate has to be on the card and read back before the old credential is superseded and revoked, with supersedes_id linking them.

patches.title: A recovery tile on the logon screen
patches.proof: 0048a's challenge and response are reachable before anybody logs in. Today they are not: the tray draws them, the tray lives in a logged-on session, and a user whose PIN is blocked cannot log on - so the mechanism built for that situation is available only to people who do not need it. One tile that authenticates nothing, not a credential provider replacement: replacing the machine's provider means a bug locks everybody out, administrator included.

patches.title: Angular shell, nginx proxy, auth
patches.proof: The console is built into an image and served by the edge under the same origin as the API: / to the console, /api to the API, deep links answered with index.html. Running in compose and on the CMS host.

patches.title: Token and cardholder inventory
patches.proof: The console lists tokens and their state. The MODEL column shows the form factor because that is all the API sends, and cardholders have no endpoint at all.

patches.title: Lifecycle actions from the console
patches.proof: The API half is finished. All five gaps in doc 11 are closed: GET /api/profiles lists what can be issued and what each profile demands of the person it is issued to; the cardholder catalogue and the directory lookup behind it landed on 2026-08-22; a failed job carries its Result into the overview; and POST /api/jobs/enrol takes a cardholderId, reads the identity from that row rather than from three loose strings, sets Job.CardholderId, and refuses an unknown profile or an identity the profile cannot use at the post rather than a minute later on an agent.
patches.gap: The page. Nothing on the console side of enrolment is built - the dialog, the person search, the confirmation that spells out the UPN and the SID before they are claimed, and AwaitingUser shown as waiting rather than as stuck. Specified in doc 11.

patches.title: Who an operator is, and what they may do
patches.proof: Five patches. The shared X-Blinky-Operator token is one secret for everybody: the audit trail cannot say who revoked a credential, there are no roles, nothing expires, and it leaks. It stays while the lab is being tested and goes when 0053e lands.

patches.title: Operator authentication by certificate
patches.proof: mTLS on the console listener against the CA that issues user certificates, not the agent CA - two populations, two anchors. The operator's identity arrives in its own header: X-Client-Verify and X-Client-Cert stay blanked on 8443, because the smoke test checks that a browser cannot forge an agent identity and passing them through would undo it.

patches.title: A session that can be ended
patches.proof: Proved on BY-CACMS on 2026-09-11: a session token reached /api/profiles with no shared operator token and got 200; POST /api/auth/sign-out returned 200; the same token on the same endpoint immediately afterwards got 401. That is the difference the patch exists for - a self-contained token would have kept working until it expired.
patches.gap: The session list and log-out-everywhere are built but have not been exercised from a console, because there is no page yet.

patches.title: Roles
patches.proof: operator, auditor, administrator. From directory group membership where there is a directory - the LDAP client already reads it and needs nothing but read - and from a local table where there is not.

patches.title: The first super-admin, and the way back in
patches.proof: Bound by the public key's thumbprint, the same strong binding demanded of certificate mappings in 0035. The bootstrap path closes after first use. And a break-glass needing physical access to the server: without one a lost super-admin card locks everybody out of the console, which is the blast radius 0049a refuses for the logon screen.

patches.title: The shared token retired
patches.proof: Proved on BY-CACMS on 2026-09-11. A person signed in through the browser - password, the installer password replaced, a second factor enrolled from a QR code and confirmed - and the account row now reads must_change_password false with the second factor confirmed. The shared token was then presented to /api/profiles and refused with 401, as was a request carrying nothing. Two live sessions survived the deployment, because a session is a row rather than a thing the process remembers. The service-credential half was never built and the reason is recorded: nothing automated ever used the token - the installer only generated it, and the revocation-list publisher reads /pki/, which is public.

patches.title: Audit browser
Agent MSI and upgrade path
patches.proof: blinky-agent MSI installs a service, a tray and its configuration, and upgraded itself in place seven times in one evening. x64, because an x86 package puts the configuration in WOW6432Node where the 64-bit agent does not look.

patches.title: blinky-samba-setup
patches.proof: The chain is published into the Samba4 directory - root in Certification Authorities, issuing CA in NTAuthCertificates - and the KDC holds a PKINIT certificate. Both verified on BY-DC01.

patches.title: Production compose profile
Documentation pass and screenshots
patches.proof: Three defects on the clone-to-logon path are fixed: provision-dc.sh orders samba-ad-dc after network-online.target and reloads it when it bound only to the loopback; resign-issuing-ca.sh is idempotent, having silently invalidated NTAuth, the workstation stores and the KDC chain three times in one day; blinky-samba-setup.sh rebuilds kdc-chain.pem around the certificate already on the controller when refreshed with --from-url alone.
patches.gap: No documentation pass and no screenshots yet. The fixes above are what a stranger following the repository would have hit, not the pass itself.

patches.title: The agent CA belongs to the deployment, and revocation is enforced at the edge
patches.proof: dev-certs.sh writes the agent CA unencrypted next to the certificates, which is right for a laptop and must never reach a customer. And a revocation list for it: an agent whose state is not Enrolled is already refused by AgentAuthenticationMiddleware - that is the defence and it works - but nothing checks a CRL at the TLS layer, so a withdrawn certificate still completes a handshake before being turned away.

patches.title: One mark for the whole product
patches.proof: brand/ holds three SVGs and build-assets.mjs, the same arrangement as BlinkyLite's. The mark is BlinkyLite's key-in-an-arc in the console's cyan (#18C9DF) with a node at each end of the arc: two products, one family, differing in the accent and the nodes rather than in the drawing. The console sidebar, the sign-in screen, the favicon, the API, the agent service and the tray icon all resolve to it; the hexagon-and-eye artwork and its source PNGs are gone. scripts/build-icons.ps1 is deleted - it built the .ico files by downscaling the 256 px drawing, so the 16 px tray icon was a smudge; the generator renders the simplified mark at 48 px and below instead. Re-running the generator leaves git status clean. A block of !important overrides at the top of frontend/src/settings.scss had repainted every primary button, active tab and eyebrow green since 0051/0052, sign-in included; it is removed, and the console's own cyan shows. 20 console tests pass, the WPF client builds with the new icon.
patches.gap: The visual unification stops at the mark. The WPF tray UI still carries its own colours rather than the console's, and the console's own stylesheet is codex's - a pass over both is not in this patch.

patches.title: One palette, generated into the console and the tray
patches.proof: tools/PaletteTool holds 29 roles in two themes as data and writes frontend/src/tokens.scss and both Blinky.Agent.Ui theme dictionaries; nothing else defines a colour. The console had 269 distinct hexes, forty of them the same green a digit apart, and the tray UI a blue that belonged to neither. Eight tests: every text pair at least 4.5:1 in both themes, both themes defining the same roles, the committed files equal to what the generator writes, every DynamicResource a view asks for present in both dictionaries, and no stylesheet or component carrying a hex of its own (one exception, the white behind a QR code, written down with its reason). Solution builds, 673 tests pass, 20 console tests pass. Sign-in, overview and settings seen in a browser in both themes.
patches.gap: The WPF tray UI was not run: its colours are checked by test and it compiles, but nobody has looked at PinDialog or TokensWindow on screen since they changed. The console pages that need data - tokens, certificates, help desk - were seen empty, because the stack does not come up (0100).

patches.title: The console's container image builds again
patches.proof: The console's build context is frontend/, and Docker reads only the .dockerignore beside the context - the repository root's never applied. COPY . . therefore copied the developer's own node_modules, which is a tree of symlinks into a pnpm store the container does not have (and on Windows not even the same kind of link), over the one pnpm had just installed; pnpm build then died on Cannot find module '/src/node_modules/@angular/cli/bin/ng.js'. It broke on every machine that had ever run pnpm install in frontend/ and nowhere else, so CI - a clean checkout - never saw it. frontend/.dockerignore fixes it. docker compose up -d --build serves the stack and ./smoke-test.sh passes all 13 checks against it, on this machine, 2026-09-30.

patches.title: One family: the console drawn as BlinkyLite's is
patches.proof: Written by cloud-ai because codex is not writing for now. Palette neutrals are BlinkyLite's in both themes, accent Blinky's cyan as one fill with near-black text, regenerated into tokens.scss and both tray themes; PaletteTests pass. Type, radii and flatness from BlinkyLite's stylesheet; shell, top bar and sign-in card rebuilt to its measures; gradients, glows, blur and upper-case labels removed. Compared side by side with BlinkyLite's console on 2026-10-08, sign-in and signed-in shell, dark and light; ng build and 20 console tests pass.
patches.gap: Signed-in pages seen with no API behind them, so populated tables, the helpdesk view and settings forms with data are unseen; the tray, which takes the same palette, has not been opened

patches.title: The console's session leaves JavaScript
patches.proof: The session token was kept in sessionStorage and sent as Authorization: Bearer, so any script on the page could read the one secret that can revoke a credential or disclose a PUK - and this console has already put a password in the address bar once, through a form that submitted natively. It is now the blinky_session cookie: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict, Path=/, expiring with the session row. The sign-in response carries who you are and not the token. CSRF is answered by double-submit - a deliberately readable blinky_csrf cookie echoed in X-Blinky-Csrf, compared in AgentAuthenticationMiddleware, 403 when absent, exempting only sign-in, totp/enrol and password, which run before a session exists. The API reads no session header any more. Shape taken from Winch's ADR 0009. Eleven new tests over the cookie flags, the comparison and the source paths that must stay closed; 683 .NET tests and 20 console tests pass, the console builds. Verified against a stack running on this machine once 0100 unblocked it: the sign-in response sets blinky_session with httponly, secure, samesite=strict and blinky_csrf without httponly, and carries no token; in the signed-in console document.cookie holds only blinky_csrf and storage only the theme; a reload keeps the shell and the operator's name; POST /api/jobs/inventory is 403 without X-Blinky-Csrf and 200 with it; Authorization: Bearer and X-Blinky-Session with the same token are both 401; sign-out expires both cookies and the old cookie is then refused.
patches.gap: Not deployed anywhere yet. The lab server still runs the old build, and everybody signed in there will be signed out once when it is updated, because their token is no longer read.

patches.title: An enrolment token is a row, not a constant
patches.proof: Blinky:Enrolment:BootstrapToken was one value in docker-compose.yml - the same secret for every machine and for the life of the deployment - and ADCS_CONNECTOR_CLIENT_FINGERPRINTS was a connector fingerprint copied into .env by hand. Both are gone. EnrolmentToken carries a name, purpose (Agent or AdcsConnector), term, max uses, uses, optional domain, creator and revocation; the value is shown once and the row holds only its SHA-256. The console has Administracja / Żetony to make, list and revoke - not edit and not delete, for the reason AuditEvent is not editable. A connector enrols through the same endpoint with a connector-purpose token and the API writes connector_registrations itself; ConnectorIdentities reads that table per request, so a withdrawal takes effect on the next call rather than at the next restart. Shape taken from Winch's EnrollmentToken. Verified on a stack on this machine: a 1-day 1-use token enrolled an agent and was refused the second time (401); an agent token presented with purpose=connector was refused; a revoked token was refused; the connector's enrolment returned its fingerprint and the row showed active; the list endpoint shows uses and carries no values; the console created a token and showed it once. 694 tests pass, 11 of them new.
patches.gap: Not deployed. The lab server runs the old build, and this is a schema change: deploying means docker compose down -v or a hand-written ALTER for enrolment_tokens and connector_registrations. Agents already enrolled are unaffected - they authenticate with certificates - but the value in the lab's .env stops working, and the ADCS connector on HZCS01 has to enrol once to get a registration row before it can collect work again. smoke-test.sh mints its own token through scripts/new-enrol-token.sh; that path ran here, but the two enrolment checks were not seen green in one run because the lab's usual ports were taken by other projects on this machine and the script's host-side call uses the same variable for the published and the internal port.

patches.title: One connector reads the CA and the directory
patches.proof: The API read Active Directory with a bind DN and svc_blinky's password in .env on a Linux host, the only process in the deployment with no domain identity; the password went with that host's .env when BY-CACMS was wiped on 2026-10-08. The ADCS connector already runs as the integration account on a domain member, so it now answers six directory routes (/connector/directory/probe, search, find, members, write-access, netbios) over the same channel as the CA, POST with the value in the body. It runs the API's own LdapDirectory with no bind DN - Negotiate from the service's Kerberos ticket, DC from the locator, naming context from RootDSE, LDAPS 636 - and drops the connection after any failure. The API's ConnectorDirectory is chosen with DIRECTORY_VIA=Connector and refuses to start without CA_BACKEND=Adcs; a pre-0104 connector's 404 is reported as too old, not as nobody found. ConnectorDirectoryTests (11) drive the API client through the polling queue into the connector's routes in memory, including LogonNames resolving AD\s.frankiewicz end to end; 821 tests pass.
patches.gap: Never run against a real domain: no bind from a real service account on a member has happened. First run is MS-CONN01.ad.digitalworkspace.pl with the connector as AD\svc_blinky; the console's directory test and one enrolment through ADCS are the check

patches.title: The agent's loopback API, and the ACL it has to replace
patches.gap: The riskiest patch in this phase. A named pipe was granted to INTERACTIVE and LocalSystem and the operating system enforced it; a loopback socket is open to every process of every user on the machine. Keeping the pipe was possible - every call goes through a Tauri command into Rust anyway, and Rust opens a pipe as easily as a socket - and was rejected for shape: the product already speaks HTTP and JSON, and a local API leaves room for something other than this one application. Four checks rebuild the guarantee, each with its own test: the connecting process resolved to a PID and refused unless it runs as the interactive user of the console session; port and token readable only by that user and SYSTEM; any Origin header refused with no CORS ever emitted; the certificate pinned by the client rather than placed in a Windows trust store.

patches.title: frontend/ becomes a library and two applications
patches.gap: A single-project Angular workspace today. Must happen before 0082: splitting it after two applications exist means moving every file twice.

patches.title: Blinky.Workstation: Angular in a Tauri v2 shell
patches.gap: Replaces the screens of Blinky.Agent.Ui, which is finished and proved on hardware - 0046, 0047, 0048 and 0048a - using the components the console uses. HTTP happens in the Rust layer behind a Tauri command and never as fetch from the WebView, because a pinned certificate cannot be checked by the browser engine. The app reaches the backend only through the agent.

patches.title: Signing in at the workstation: Kerberos, or a password
patches.gap: Kerberos is already the design in doc 05; the password is the new part, for a machine with no domain. Verified at the backend and never by the agent, hashed with a per-user salt, rate-limited and lockable per account.

patches.title: Enrolment the person started
patches.gap: No window appears that nobody asked for. The ceremony is reachable only from an application already in front of somebody and waits as long as the person needs. 0049 folds in here.

patches.title: The same ceremony, driven by an operator
patches.gap: Needs 0023a underneath it, and inherits whatever 0086 decides about who an operator is.

patches.title: The admin panel's way in: a bootstrap superadmin, password and TOTP
patches.proof: Proved end to end on BY-CACMS on 2026-09-11. A wrong password is refused; the installer-generated one is accepted once and asks for a real one; the old one stops working the moment it is replaced; the new one then asks for a second factor; enrolling returns a secret and an otpauth URI; and signing in with the code from that secret returns a session naming the administrator. A defect only that run could find: the endpoint returned totp-enrolment-required before looking at the code, so a secret could be handed out and never confirmed and the account could never finish signing in. The state machine was right the whole time and every unit test was green, because they checked the rule and not the branch beside it.

patches.title: TOTP, properly: enrolment, drift, recovery codes
patches.gap: A code accepted once and not again inside its window, a stated drift tolerance and no more, recovery codes shown once and stored hashed. Without them the first lost telephone is a break-glass event.

patches.title: FIDO2 as an operator second factor
patches.gap: The CTAP2 work of 0070-0076 turned on ourselves. Deliberately after phase 7 and deliberately not built twice.

patches.title: Full CRUD for the models the panel manages
patches.gap: Everything describing configuration or people gets all five. Everything recording an event - AuditEvent, Job, Credential, PUK disclosures - gets create-and-transition, asserted by a test rather than left to the next reviewer to remember.

patches.title: Blinky.Agent.Ui is removed
patches.gap: Deleted in one commit once 0082 and 0084 do everything 0046 through 0048a do, and not a patch earlier: two clients on one local API means two places to fix the same defect.

patches.title: Blinky.Fido: CTAP2 over HID, AuthenticatorInfo, joined to the token by serial
patches.proof: Blinky.Fido on Yubico.YubiKey 1.18.0: IFidoKey and its Yubico adapter read AAGUID, CTAP versions, FIDO2 PIN set and retries, discoverable slots left and CTAP 2.1 controls, and open a key by serial. Denied HID access is an error naming elevation, from the SDK's own exception seen on 2026-10-08.
patches.gap: Not in the inventory and not joined to the PC/SC token; no key has been read through it

patches.title: The FIDO application in the inventory and on the token page
patches.proof: Not started. Two PIN retry counters, never one. The API half is cloud-ai, the page is codex.

patches.title: FIDO PIN set and change, and FIDO reset
patches.proof: PIN set, change, minimum length and forced change enforced in the service inside provisioning; IFidoKey.Reset in the adapter.
patches.gap: No standalone PIN-change or reset job, so no confirmation naming what a reset destroys and no power-up window handling; nothing run on a key

patches.title: Blinky.Passkeys: IPasskeyDirectory, PasskeyCreationOptions, Capabilities, EntraPasskeyDirectory
patches.proof: IPasskeyDirectory (find, begin, complete, cancel, list, delete) and EntraPasskeyDirectory on Graph v1.0, ported in semantics from KeyEnroll. Graph's answer normalises into PasskeyCreationOptions with rpId and origin taken from it; a test moves rp.id and the origin follows, another fails on a login.microsoft.com literal in src/ outside the Entra class. Client credentials by certificate or secret via one RFC 7523 assertion shared with Okta, no MSAL. 401 refreshed once, 429 waited out within 30 s, Graph's error text and status surfaced. 44 tests across 0073 and 0073a.
patches.gap: Fixtures are synthesised from Graph's documentation and KeyEnroll's tests, not recorded; no tenant reached, so v1.0 versus beta, challengeTimeoutInMinutes, the x5t certificate assertion and the application permissions are unproved

patches.title: OktaPasskeyDirectory, Factors route
patches.proof: OktaPasskeyDirectory on the Factors route. Activation in standard base64 under Okta's names; rpId defaults to the org host and an rp.id in the answer wins, custom domain included; user handle decoded as Okta's sign-in page does. A ceremony failed on purpose deletes the pending factor, as does a factor whose options cannot be read; a factor not ACTIVE after activation is a failure. SSWS token or private_key_jwt (RS256/ES256, kid).
patches.gap: No Okta org reached from here; KeyEnroll's hardware run on Okta is evidence for the shapes, not for this code. That 0077 always cancels an incomplete begin is 0077's to prove

patches.title: Contracts: ProvisionFido2Credential envelopes and a protocol version bump
patches.proof: Prepare (the job's single step), Ready, Ceremony and Result plus the provider's verdict in Blinky.Contracts/Fido2Contracts.cs; the agent starts every exchange. CeremonyId derived from job and challenge, so one challenge is one ceremony. Version 2 for ProvisionFido2Credential only, every other envelope stays at 1 via Protocol.VersionFor. JobType numbers pinned. No contract can carry a PIN, checked by reflection. 17 tests.
patches.gap: No agent built before this commit has been sent a version-2 job; the refusal is the existing version check, tested in this build. The endpoints are 0077's

patches.title: PasskeyCredential: entity, mapping, generated schema
patches.proof: Fourth state machine enforced in the entity: MoveTo refuses a move the lifecycle does not allow and leaves the row as it was; Failed and Revoked need a reason. Schema generated by tools/SchemaTool. A test on the NHibernate mapping fails if any column but the boolean pin_set_by_agent has pin in its name. SchemaTool --roundtrip, now validating first and writing a passkey row, passed on 2026-10-08 against a throwaway PostgreSQL 17 loaded from 001-schema.sql. 14 tests.
patches.gap: API and worker not started against the new schema. Deployed databases, BY-CACMS included, need the passkey_credentials table and its foreign key applied by hand, or down -v

patches.title: The makeCredential ceremony in the agent
patches.proof: Fido2Provisioner behind the ProvisionFido2Credential step: clientDataJSON byte-exact, attestationObject from the key's own authData and statement bytes, minimum PIN length before and forced change after the provider accepts, FIDO2-labelled prompts, operator-chosen PIN without CTAP 2.1. 38 tests against a software CTAP 2.1 key that refuses a ceremony while a forced change is pending; identical calls under two provider tags.
patches.gap: The hardware milestone: no key on the workstation on 2026-10-08, so the Yubico adapter has never run and no mock relying party has seen a credential

patches.title: Api orchestration, REST, drift and revocation
patches.proof: PasskeyProvisioningService behind POST /api/jobs/fido2, GET /api/passkeys/directories, GET /api/passkeys, POST /api/passkeys/{id}/revoke and the agent's /api/jobs/{id}/fido2/ready and /fido2/result. User resolved before a job exists; challenge asked for only on Ready, deadline the sooner of provider's and job's; a repeated Ready cancels the challenge it replaces; clientDataJSON checked against issued challenge and origin before the provider sees it; row saved Provisioned before registration; refusal cancels and fails; expiry is a retryable 409 back to KeyReady; same result twice registers once; job ending with an open ceremony cancels it; revocation deletes at the provider first, 404 recorded as already gone; drift listing with MissingAtProvider, StillAtProvider and ProviderOnly. 19 tests.
patches.gap: API started on 2026-10-08 against a throwaway PostgreSQL 17 (schema valid, Okta built from configuration, new routes refuse unauthenticated calls), but no ceremony has run end to end and no tenant or org has been reached; the flow is tested with an in-memory store and a scripted provider. A job expired by the watchdog does not cancel its ceremony - the worker has no provider access - and the leftover shows in the drift listing instead

tokens.what: HID Crescendo Key V3, HID C4000
tokens.note: Recognised as unsupported with a reason (0019). Only the Yubico extensions have been measured on them.

vendorSdk.shape: A managed .NET library (CrescendoDLL, net8.0 with RollForward LatestMajor, so it loads under .NET 10) over PCSC, HidSharpCore, BouncyCastle and Newtonsoft.Json, plus a CLI. LEGAL/Redist.txt makes the SDK API and CLI Tool folders redistributable.
vendorSdk.canDo: A full PIV surface - PIVGenerateKeyPair, PIVGetCertificate, PIVPutPKIData, PIVSignData, PIVDeleteKey, ACR changes, ChangePIN, ResetPINTries, PUKPut, NewToken - and a deep FIDO2/CTAP2 surface including ForceChangePin, enterprise attestation, bio enrollment and large blobs.
vendorSdk.cannotDo: No PIV attestation of any kind: every Attestation class in it is FIDO/WebAuthn. And Crescendo has no PIV management key at all - access is governed by ACRs plus the PIN, and NewToken personalises the card on its own terms.
vendorSdk.constraints: Four that shape any future support, from the API reference and the CLI's own help text. Key references are 0x9A plus vendor slots B0, B4 and F0, addressed alongside standard PIV BER-TLV tags such as 5FC105 - so the data objects are PIV and the slot map is not. Key generation offers RSA2048, RSA3072, RSA4096, CURVEP256 and CURVEP384, and nothing else: no Ed25519, no X25519, so a profile has to pick an algorithm both a YubiKey and a Crescendo will accept or say which card it is for. Access control rules can be changed only on Crescendo 4000 (applet V4) and only on a slot or object that is completely empty, which inverts Blinky's order of operations - rules first, then the key, where today the key comes first and the certificate follows. And piv-pki-put writes a private key, a certificate or both, so a key can arrive on one of these cards from outside, which is the situation attestation exists to detect and the reason its absence is not a detail.
vendorSdk.consequence: Supporting these cards is a capability-model change, not a driver. Blinky refuses to ask a CA to sign without an attestation chaining to a pinned root, and its personalisation is management-key diversification; neither has a Crescendo equivalent. The SDK is not needed to talk to the card - the issuance path is standard SP 800-73, which Blinky.Piv already speaks. It is worth having as an independent oracle for what SP 800-73 does not describe, and as a reference for the FIDO half of phase 7.

instructionSplit.standard: 00A4 SELECT, 0020 VERIFY, 0024 CHANGE REFERENCE DATA, 002C RESET RETRY COUNTER, 00CB GET DATA, 00DB PUT DATA, 0087 GENERAL AUTHENTICATE, 0047 GENERATE ASYMMETRIC KEY PAIR
instructionSplit.yubicoOnly: 00FD GET VERSION, 00F8 GET SERIAL, 00F7 GET METADATA, 00F9 ATTEST, 00FF SET MANAGEMENT KEY, MOVE KEY
instructionSplit.note: The whole issuance path - generate, sign the request on the card, write the certificate back, PIN and unblock - is in the standard set. What a foreign card cannot give is attestation, its own serial and metadata, and mutual authentication against key 9B. That is measurement waiting to be done, not a conclusion.
